📖 Executive Summary - Regulatory Compliance Framework

Healthcare benefits administration operates under strict federal oversight, requiring compliance with RegulatoryAgency tax code (IRC §223, §125), PrivacyRegulation privacy rules (45 CFR §164.312), PaymentSecurity payment card security (v4.0), and BenefitsRegulation disclosure mandates. The RA Domain enforces these regulations algorithmically, embedding compliance rules directly into domain services.

This dashboard details the four-pillar regulatory framework, identifies nine P0 compliance gaps with $500k-$2M risk exposure, and explains the audit trail architecture supporting 7-year data retention requirements.

🏛️ Four-Pillar Regulatory Framework

1️⃣ RegulatoryAgency Tax Code Requirements (Healthcare Account Regulations)

Internal Revenue Code §223 (HealthSavings), §125 (FlexAccount), and RegulatoryAgency Publication 969 establish contribution limits, rollover rules, and qualified expense categories. For 2024-2025, limits are:

  • FlexAccount: $3,200 annual maximum with $640 rollover cap OR 2.5-month grace period (mutually exclusive)
  • HealthSavings: $4,150 individual / $8,300 family with 100% unlimited rollover plus $1,000 catch-up for age 55+
  • DependentCare FlexAccount: $5,000 with zero rollover (use-it-or-lose-it)

The platform's CarryoverDollarsDomainService enforces these limits algorithmically: Min(accountBalance, $640) for FlexAccount, accountBalance * 1.0 for HealthSavings, and employerDefinedLimit for HealthReimbursement.

⚠️ COMPLIANCE GAPS IDENTIFIED (P0 Priority):

  • P0-001: No code verification of FlexAccount $3,200 annual contribution limit
  • P0-002: No code verification of HealthSavings $4,150/$8,300 annual contribution limits
  • P0-003: No enforcement of FlexAccount $640 rollover cap
  • P0-004: DependentCare FlexAccount may incorrectly allow rollover instead of full expiration
  • P0-005: Cosmetic surgery expenses not automatically rejected per RegulatoryAgency Publication 502 ineligible expense list

Risk Exposure: RegulatoryAgency penalties of $50-$2,000 per violation. Enterprise-wide exposure if systematic errors affect thousands of accounts.

2️⃣ PrivacyRegulation Security Rule (Protected Health Information)

45 CFR §164.312 mandates administrative, physical, and technical safeguards for Protected Health Information (PHI), which includes account balances, request details, transaction history, and customer demographics. The platform implements:

  • Access Control: Multi-factor authentication (MFA) for administrator logins
  • Audit Trail: BalanceChangeAudit entity captures all PHI access with user, timestamp, and action
  • Encryption: TLS 1.2+ for data in transit, AES-256 for data at rest
  • Session Management: 10-15 minute inactivity timeout

P0-008: Requires validation that audit trail completeness meets §164.312(b) requirements for logging all PHI access, create, modify, and delete operations. PrivacyRegulation violations trigger OCR investigations with penalties of $100-$50,000 per violation, potentially millions in aggregate for systematic gaps.

3️⃣ PaymentSecurity Payment Card Security (Card Transaction Data)

The Card and CardTransaction entities place the platform within PaymentSecurity scope, requiring compliance with Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard v4.0. Critical requirements include:

  • CVV Prohibition: Never store CVV/CVC codes (card security codes)
  • PAN Encryption: Encrypt Primary Account Number (PAN) using AES-256 encryption at rest
  • Display Masking: Show only last 4 digits (XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-1234)
  • Tokenization: Tokenize card-on-file data for recurring transactions

P0-006, P0-007: Requires code-level validation that CVV storage prohibition is enforced and PAN encryption is implemented. PaymentSecurity violations trigger payment network fines of $5,000-$25,000 per month until remediated, plus potential suspension of card processing capabilities.

4️⃣ BenefitsRegulation Disclosure Requirements (Employee Benefits Law)

Employee Retirement Income Security Act mandates participant disclosure for welfare benefit plans, including payment accounts. The platform must generate RegulatoryAgency Form 5500 annual reports and provide Summary Plan Descriptions (SPD) to participants.

Analysis of the CarryoverDollarsDomainService reveals a method referencing Form 5500 generation, but incomplete BenefitsRegulation participant disclosure implementation has been flagged. Non-compliance risks Department of Labor penalties and plan disqualification.

📋 Audit Trail & 7-Year Data Retention

Regulatory requirements mandate 7-year retention of all financial transactions and healthcare records. The BalanceChangeAudit and RolloverTransferTracking entities provide comprehensive transaction lineage, capturing:

  • Transaction Correlation IDs: Link related operations (rollover → balance update → event publication)
  • User Attribution: System vs. administrator vs. customer-initiated changes
  • Timestamp Precision: Millisecond granularity for forensic investigation
  • Reason Codes: Business context (year-end rollover, manual adjustment, request payment)

This audit architecture supports regulatory examinations, internal audits, and customer dispute resolution. All audit logs are immutable—no updates or deletes permitted—ensuring data integrity for compliance inquiries.
